chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazzaz, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim al-Darimi, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace:
That a man freed part of his slave, so Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'He is free, not for God has a partner.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ لِلَّهِ شَرِيكٌ: not for God has a partner

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say when a man freed part of his slave?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) rules that partial manumission of a slave results in the slave becoming fully free, invoking the phrase 'Laysa lillahi sharikun' to emphasize the absolute and indivisible nature of God's authority over emancipation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that manumission is a definitive act of liberation, reflecting the theological concept that just as God has no partner, the slave's status transitions completely from bondage to freedom. The incident highlights the practical application of divine sovereignty in social transactions, linking legal emancipation to spiritual purity.
